To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CADM1 mediates adhesion between mast cells and sensory neurons and that this interaction enhances mast cell responsiveness to stimuli.
Mast cells and sensory neurons express the adhesion molecule CADM1 and form a functional adhesive bond which promotes mast cell secretion of inflammatory mediators in response to antigen stimulation.

CADM1 dependent adhesion of mast cells to sensory neuron nerve endings enhances mast cell responsiveness to antigens, this may explain the increased incidence of pain associated disorders such as IBS in patients with allergies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cell-cell adhesion in the pathophysiological processes underlying chronic inflammatory diseases.
the interaction of mast cells and sensory neurons and the effect of this interaction on the secretion of inflammatory mediators.
the role of CADM1 dependent mast cell sensory neuron interactions in the pathophysiological processes of chronic pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data show that mast cells and sensory neurons interact through the adhesion molecule CADM1, this interaction enhances mast cell responses to antigen and could explain the increased incidence of neuroinflammatory disorders in atopic patients.

the data presented in this thesis show that mast cells and sensory neurons are capable of interacting in a CADM1 dependent manner and that the adhesion of mast cells to sensory neuron axons enhances mast cell responsiveness to stimulation.
CADM1 dependent adhesion between mast cells and sensory neurons is a key component of the neuroimmune cross talk which drives mast cell activation in response to antigen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CADM1 dependent mast cell adhesion to sensory neurons enhances mast cell responses to antigen and promotes the development of a neuroinflammatory environment.
CADM1 dependent mast cell sensory neuron interactions may be important for normal immune responses, but when dysregulated could lead to neuroinflammation and pain in atopic patients.

CADM1 dependent adhesion between mast cells and sensory neurons promotes the secretion of inflammatory mediators by mast cells, which could be important in the pathogenesis of atopic diseases and neuroinflammatory disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mast cells can be activated by sensory neurons via CADM1, which could explain why atopic individuals are more susceptible to developing painful neuroinflammatory diseases.
CADM1 dependent adhesion between mast cells and sensory neurons is functionally relevant and that this interaction may contribute to the pathogenesis of atopic disorders.
CADM1 dependent adhesion between mast cells and sensory neurons is a novel and important component of neuroimmune interactions.
